title: Descent of a syntomic algebra map along a directed colimit of base rings
statement: Let $I$ be a nonempty directed set and $(R_i)_{i\in I}$ a directed system of commutative rings, with compatible unital transition homomorphisms $R_i\to R_j$ for $i\leq j$, and colimit $R=\varinjlim_i R_i$ in commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Fix $i_0\in I$, commutative $R_{i_0}$-algebras $B_0,C_0$, and an $R_{i_0}$-algebra homomorphism $\varphi_0:B_0\to C_0$ of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. For $i\geq i_0$ set $B_i=R_i\otimes_{R_{i_0}}B_0$, $C_i=R_i\otimes_{R_{i_0}}C_0$, and let $\varphi_i=1\otimes\varphi_0:B_i\to C_i$; put $B=R\otimes_{R_{i_0}}B_0$, $C=R\otimes_{R_{i_0}}C_0$ and $\varphi=1\otimes\varphi_0:B\to C$. Assume that $\varphi$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], of finite presentation, and that for every prime $\mathfrak p\subset B$ its fibre ring $C\otimes_B\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is a local complete intersection over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field]. Then there exists $i\geq i_0$ such that $\varphi_i$ is flat, of finite presentation, and for every prime $\mathfrak p_i\subset B_i$ the fibre ring $C_i\otimes_{B_i}\kappa(\mathfrak p_i)$ is a local complete intersection over $\kappa(\mathfrak p_i)$. No finite-presentation assumption on $R_{i_0}\to B_0$ or $R_{i_0}\to C_0$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0C33 (lemma-colimit-lci), syntomic case, with Tag 00SL (definition-lci) expanded as flat, finite presentation, and local-complete-intersection residue-field fibres.

proof.text: Work over the tail $i\geq i_0$. For $T_0=B_0$ and $T_0=C_0$, the squares $R_i\to R_i\otimes_{R_{i_0}}T_0$, $R\to R\otimes_{R_{i_0}}T_0$ are pushouts by [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]: maps out of the tensor product are exactly pairs of ring maps agreeing on $R_{i_0}$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-limit-finite-presentation-colimits] to obtain $B=\varinjlim B_i$ and $C=\varinjlim C_i$. The same argument applies on every later tail. Tensor associativity identifies $C_i$ with $B_i\otimes_{B_0}C_0$: $(r\otimes b)\otimes c\mapsto r\otimes\varphi_0(b)c$, with inverse $r\otimes c\mapsto(r\otimes1)\otimes c$. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-base-change-composition](1) shows that every $B_i\to C_i$ is finitely presented. All indexing categories here are small directed tails of the given set, in a universe containing the rings.

source.place: Tag 0C33 (lemma-colimit-lci), notation and use of Tag 00QO; Tag 00R0 (lemma-limit-finite-presentation); Tag 05G5 (lemma-base-change-finiteness)(4).

proof.text: For each prime $\mathfrak q\subset C$, put $\mathfrak p=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$ and $F=C\otimes_B\kappa(\mathfrak p)$. Flatness of $B\to C$ gives flatness of $B_{\mathfrak p}\to C_{\mathfrak q}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-ring-maps]. The prime $\mathfrak Q=\ker(F\to\kappa(\mathfrak q))$ belongs to some $D(h)$ in the defining complete-intersection cover of $F$, so $h\notin\mathfrak Q$ and $F_h$ is a global complete intersection by [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-syntomic-at-prime-relative-global-complete-intersection] to $B\to C$ with the finite-presentation neighbourhood $g=1$. Its three hypotheses are precisely the finite presentation assumed in the item, the local flatness just obtained, and this choice of $h$. It gives $g_{\mathfrak q}\notin\mathfrak q$ and a specified relative global complete-intersection presentation of $C_{g_{\mathfrak q}}$ over $B$.

source.place: Tag 0C33, syntomic paragraph, first sentence; Tag 00SY (lemma-syntomic), implication (3) to (2); Tag 00HT (lemma-flat-localization)(6).

proof.text: The opens $D(g_{\mathfrak q})$ cover $\operatorname{Spec}C$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-basic-opens-unit-ideal-quasi-compact](iii), choose a finite subcover $D(g_1),\ldots,D(g_m)$. By its clause (i), choose $h_1,\ldots,h_m\in C$ with $\sum_{a=1}^m h_ag_a=1$. Keep the presentations $C_{g_a}\cong B[x_1,\ldots,x_{n_a}]/(f_{a,1},\ldots,f_{a,c_a})$ supplied by Step 2. Empty spectra cause no exception: the finite subcover can be empty, and its unit-ideal relation is $0=1$ in $C=0$.

source.place: Tag 0C33, syntomic paragraph: elements generating the unit ideal.

proof.text: Apply [lemma-nagata-filtered-colimit-finite-data] to $C=\varinjlim_{i\geq i_0}C_i$ from Step 1, the finitely many $g_a,h_a$, and the one equation $\sum_a h_ag_a=1$. We obtain a stage $j\geq i_0$ and lifts $g_{j,a},h_{j,a}\in C_j$ such that $\sum_a h_{j,a}g_{j,a}=1$. Write $g_{k,a}$ for their images for $k\geq j$. The relation persists under every transition homomorphism, so these elements generate the unit ideal at every later stage, including when $m=0$.

source.place: Tag 0C33, syntomic paragraph: lifting the cover and its unit-ideal relation; Tags 00D6 and 00D7, directed-colimit finite relations.

proof.text: Fix $a\in\{1,\ldots,m\}$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection-noetherian-approximation] to the specified presentation of $C_{g_a}$ in Step 3. It supplies a finite type integer subring $P_a\subset B$ containing the coefficients and a relative global complete intersection $Q_a=P_a[x_1,\ldots,x_{n_a}]/(f_{a,1},\ldots,f_{a,c_a})$. By [lem-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection-base-change](a), the presentation identifies $B\otimes_{P_a}Q_a\cong C_{g_a}$ as $B$-algebras. Moreover $P_a$ is finitely presented over $\mathbf Z$: choose a surjection $\mathbf Z[t_1,\ldots,t_r]\twoheadrightarrow P_a$ using its finite ring generators; [lem-trf-mvpolynomial-noetherian] says its kernel is finitely generated. This is a finite presentation by [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. The displayed presentation also makes $Q_a$ finitely presented over $P_a$.

source.place: Tag 0C33, relative-global-complete-intersection paragraph, first two sentences; Tag 00SU (lemma-relative-global-complete-intersection-Noetherian); Tag 00SS (lemma-base-change-relative-global-complete-intersection)(1).

proof.text: Put $D_{j,a}=(C_j)_{g_{j,a}}$. This is a finitely presented $B_j$-algebra: take a finite presentation $C_j=B_j[x_1,\ldots,x_N]/(u_1,\ldots,u_s)$ from Step 1, lift $g_{j,a}$ to a polynomial $G$, and adjoin one variable $t$ and the relation $Gt-1$. The maps $x_b\mapsto x_b/1$, $t\mapsto1/g_{j,a}$ give the isomorphism with $D_{j,a}$, with inverse determined by the invertibility of $G$; thus this is a presentation in [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. By [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-localization-away-base-change] and the tensor pushout property of Step 1, $R\otimes_{R_j}D_{j,a}\cong C_{g_a}$ as $B$-algebras, via $r\otimes(c/g_{j,a}^e)\mapsto(r\otimes c)/g_a^e$. The analogous formula with $R_k$ gives $R_k\otimes_{R_j}D_{j,a}\cong(C_k)_{g_{k,a}}$ for $k\geq j$.

source.place: Tag 0C33, syntomic paragraph, application of the relative-global-complete-intersection case to principal localizations.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-model-stage] to the original ring diagram $R_i$ with starting index $j$, $R_j$-algebras $B_j,D_{j,a}$ and their finitely presented map from Step 6, and the rings $P_a,Q_a$ from Step 5. The canonical isomorphism $R\otimes_{R_j}B_j\cong B$ equips its left side with the required $P_a$-algebra structure. Combining Steps 5 and 6 gives the required comparison $B\otimes_{P_a}Q_a\cong R\otimes_{R_j}D_{j,a}$, compatible with the inclusion of $B$ because both comparisons are $B$-algebra maps. All hypotheses of the model-stage node hold: $P_a$ is finitely presented over $\mathbf Z$, $Q_a$ over $P_a$, and $B_j\to D_{j,a}$ is finitely presented. It supplies $k_a\geq j$, a map $P_a\to B_{k_a}$, and a $B_{k_a}$-algebra isomorphism $B_{k_a}\otimes_{P_a}Q_a\cong(C_{k_a})_{g_{k_a,a}}$, using Step 6 to identify the target. By [lem-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection-base-change](b), this last algebra is a relative global complete intersection over $B_{k_a}$.

source.place: Tag 0C33, relative-global-complete-intersection paragraph, descent of the comparison isomorphism using Tags 00QO and 0C32; syntomic paragraph, penultimate sentence.

proof.text: Choose one upper bound $i$ of $j$ and the finitely many $k_a$ in the directed set. For each $a$, base-change the presentation obtained in Step 7 along $B_{k_a}\to B_i$. Its target is $(C_i)_{g_{i,a}}$: the tensor pushout identifications of Step 1 identify the base change of $C_{k_a}$ with $C_i$, and [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-localization-away-base-change] then identifies the localized algebras, sending $(c/g_{k_a,a}^e)\otimes b$ to $b\bar c/g_{i,a}^e$. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection-base-change](b) shows that every $B_i\to(C_i)_{g_{i,a}}$ is a relative global complete intersection. The identity $\sum_a h_{i,a}g_{i,a}=1$ still holds by Step 4. If $m=0$ choose $i=j$; that identity says $C_i=0$.

source.place: Tag 0C33, syntomic paragraph: increase the index for all finitely many charts; Tag 00SS(1).

proof.text: Each chart $(C_i)_{g_{i,a}}$ is flat over $B_i$ by [lem-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection-flat], applied to its presentation from Step 8. For any prime $\mathfrak q\subset C_i$, the unit-ideal relation gives an $a$ with $g_{i,a}\notin\mathfrak q$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-localization-away-basic-open](ii), it corresponds to a prime $\mathfrak q'$ of $(C_i)_{g_{i,a}}$. Let $\mathfrak p$ be its contraction to $B_i$. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-ring-maps] the map $(B_i)_{\mathfrak p}\to((C_i)_{g_{i,a}})_{\mathfrak q'}$ is flat. The latter target identifies with $(C_i)_{\mathfrak q}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-of-localization]: both invert exactly the elements outside $\mathfrak q$, and $g_{i,a}$ is already invertible there. These are isomorphisms over $(B_i)_{\mathfrak p}$. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-flat-map-local-criterion] proves $B_i\to C_i$ flat. For $C_i=0$ there are no primes and that same criterion applies vacuously.

source.place: Tag 0C33, final sentence; Tag 00SO (lemma-local-syntomic), flatness clause; Tag 00HT(6).

proof.text: Fix a prime $\mathfrak p\subset B_i$ and write $k=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, $F=C_i\otimes_{B_i}k$. By Step 1 and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-base-change-composition](1), $F$ is finitely presented, hence finitely generated, over $k$. Applying the fibre ring map to Step 4's relation gives $\sum_a\bar h_{i,a}\bar g_{i,a}=1$, so the $D(\bar g_{i,a})$ cover $\operatorname{Spec}F$ by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-basic-opens-unit-ideal-quasi-compact](i). By [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-localization-away-base-change], $F_{\bar g_{i,a}}\cong (C_i)_{g_{i,a}}\otimes_{B_i}k$. Base-change the presentation in Step 8 using [lem-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection-base-change]. It presents this fibre as a polynomial quotient over $k$ of dimension $n-c$ whenever nonzero, by [def-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection]; if zero it is allowed as well. Thus every chart is a global complete intersection, and the displayed cover makes $F$ a local complete intersection by [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field]. An empty cover has $F=0$ and satisfies the same definition. Together with Steps 1 and 9 this proves all three asserted properties at $i\geq i_0$, without imposing any finite-presentation assumption on $R_{i_0}\to B_0$ or $R_{i_0}\to C_0$.

source.place: Tag 0C33, final sentence; Tag 00SO (lemma-local-syntomic), fibre clause; Tags 00SP and 00S9, definitions of the two complete-intersection conditions.

Statement: it matches Stacks 0C33 (algebra.tex 47706) in the syntomic case, with syntomic spelled out from 00SL (line 36437) as flat, finitely presented, and every fibre ring a local complete intersection. No hypothesis is weakened; the extra 'phi finitely presented' assumption is redundant but harmless. Steps 1-10 checked against their cited statements. Step 1 needs no finite-presentation hypothesis in the colimit node, the tail is cofinal, and finite presentation comes from base change (05G5). Step 2 meets all three hypotheses of the 00SY node, with g=1. Steps 3-4: quasi-compactness gives a finite cover, and the unit-ideal relation lifts to a stage. Step 5: the 00SU subring P_a is finitely presented over Z because Z[t] is Noetherian; 00SS(a) gives the B-algebra isomorphism. Step 6: the localization presentation and its base change are correct. Step 7: every hypothesis of the existing model-stage node holds with i0:=j, and its compatibility clause makes the stage isomorphism B_k-linear; 00SS(b) then gives a relative global complete intersection. This replaces Stacks' 00QO/0C32 argument with an existing node. Step 8: base change to a common upper bound is correct. Step 9: flatness via 00SW, 00HT(6) and localization-of-localization; I checked that U equals C_i minus q. Step 10: the fibre charts become relative global complete intersections over a field, hence global complete intersections, hence the fibre is a local complete intersection. Edge cases: C=0 / empty cover, a one-element index set, non-injective transition maps, B_0 and C_0 not finitely generated. No new nodes and no duplicates (grep over the DAG for 0C33, syntomic, and colimit plus complete intersection). No SGA. Not a target node, so the base-change-morphism and coefficient-category checks do not apply. All 15 declared tool uses are generic commutative algebra and accepted. No unit or chapter change.
